newsitem.title: USA: Earthgrains sets small share buy-sell plan.
newsitem.headline: Earthgrains sets small share buy-sell plan.

text.p: Earthgrains Co said Friday it set a buy-sell program for small shareholders.
The program enables stockholders with fewer than 100 shares of common stock as of December 27 to buy shares to reach 100 shares or to sell all of their shares.
The buy-sell program, administered by the Shareholder Communications Corp of New York, is voluntary and expires February 10, 1997, unless extended by the company.
Participants will pay a processing fee of $0.90 a share, up to a maximum of $40, it said.
A uniform market-based price per share will apply.
Shares will be bought or sold on the open market through a designated broker. Earthgrains said it will neither buy nor sell any of the shares.
The company said many Earthgrains stockholders with fewer than 100 shares received their holdings as a result of the spin-off from Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc in March 1996.
Earthgrains is the third-largest producer of fresh baked goods and the second-largest producer of refrigerated dough products in the United States.
